date_cue_surface_label: Example State official voter-information date-cue and byline policy
delivery_role_note: Visible publication/update labels, structured freshness signals, timezone-aware update precision, and archive posture shape whether official voter-information pages look current for the right reason before and after click-through.
visible_date_policy_note: Volatile official voter-information pages carry a labeled visible freshness cue such as Published or Last updated rather than leaving currentness to unlabeled template timestamps.
structured_date_policy_note: Machine-readable freshness signals are kept consistent with the visible label and are used to help search systems infer publication or significant-update time rather than to contradict the visible page.
page_vs_event_date_boundary_note: The office keeps page freshness dates distinct from election/event dates described on the page so the result cue and the voter-action date do not silently collapse into one another.
timezone_precision_note: Pages that can change near daily cutoffs preserve correct timezone-aware machine-readable update precision even when the visible label remains simpler.
historical_archive_posture_note: Historical or superseded pages are labeled and routed so archive, migration, or template timestamps do not make old instructions look newly operative.
meaningful_update_policy_note: A visible freshness change should correspond to a material public-answer change rather than cosmetic footer, analytics, or theme churn.
